subject.title: [Bug]: Memory dreaming narrative/REM lane is given apply_patch and misuses it

question: Should OpenClaw extend the plugin subagent contract so memory-core can run Dream Diary narrative subagents with no tools or an explicit allowlist?
rationale: This changes a plugin/runtime/gateway protocol boundary and a security-sensitive tool policy path, so automation should not pick the permanent API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add typed subagent tool scoping
options.body: Extend the plugin subagent/gateway agent-run path with a no-tools or explicit `toolsAllow` control, then update memory-core narrative runs and tests to use it.

options.title: Use prompt-only mitigation
options.body: Tighten the Dream Diary prompt/model guidance without changing tool policy, reducing log noise but leaving the mutating tool exposure in place.

options.title: Defer as accepted log noise
options.body: Keep the current fallback behavior and accept occasional invalid `apply_patch` logs until broader subagent API work is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Add typed subagent tool scoping
recommendation.body: Extend the plugin subagent/gateway agent-run path with a no-tools or explicit `toolsAllow` control, then update memory-core narrative runs and tests to use it.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame on the current memory-core narrative and embedded tool-allowlist paths makes this the best available routing candidate for the API-shape decision.
